+//! Corrupt-file corpus of the port's native B-rep reader (M12.1 stage 3):
+//! blank, foreign, truncated and field-corrupted `.smb` files through the
+//! raw reader and the seam's importer. Never a panic, never a hang (every
+//! case runs under a time bound); the importer hands out a model only when
+//! the edit left it whole, and then exactly the closed-form 10-box.
+//! Provenance: our own corpus, shaped after the Prime Directive's
+//! degenerate-input list; edits are made on the port's own writer output.
+//!
+//! Gate map (M12.1): covers camcraft_kernel::solidcore_import (read_smb,
+//! import_smb, the heal guards).
+
+mod smb_util;
+
+use camcraft_kernel::solidcore_impl::SolidcoreKernel;
+use camcraft_kernel::solidcore_import::{MAX_SMB_BYTES, import_smb, read_smb};
+use camcraft_kernel::{Kernel, KernelError, Measure};
+use smb_util::{bounded, box_text, edit_record, gapped_box, port_verdict};
+use solidcore::topology::Brep;
+
+/// Edits that leave the model itself whole: the importer must hand out the
+/// exact 10-box (volume AND bounding box). A dropped final newline loses
+/// nothing; a zero or negative zone tolerance is replaced by the reader's
+/// default, and the importer says so in a pinned note. A future format
+/// version is NOT intact: the seam refuses it (decision 5).
+const INTACT: &[&str] = &[
+    "last byte dropped",
+    "zero zone tolerance",
+    "negative zone tolerance",
+];
+
+/// Corrupt native files: each name, the raw reader's verdict and the
+/// importer's verdict, pinned so a port bump that changes any of them fails
+/// here and gets looked at. Every importer verdict outside [`INTACT`] must
+/// be an `Err` - the importer never hands out a corrupt model.
+fn corpus() -> Vec<(&'static str, Vec<u8>)> {
+    let t = box_text();
+    let b = t.as_bytes();
+    let cut = |num: usize, den: usize| b.get(..b.len() * num / den).unwrap_or_default().to_vec();
+    let noise: Vec<u8> = (0u32..4096)
+        .map(|i| (i.wrapping_mul(2_654_435_761) >> 13) as u8)
+        .collect();
+    vec![
+        ("empty file", Vec::new()),
+        ("one space", b" ".to_vec()),
+        (
+            "text, not a B-rep",
+            b"solid cube\nfacet normal 0 0 1\n".to_vec(),
+        ),
+        ("binary noise 4 KiB", noise),
+        ("header only", b"Version 42\nHealer Version 10\n".to_vec()),
+        (
+            "future version",
+            t.replacen("Version 42", "Version 9999", 1).into_bytes(),
+        ),
+        ("cut at 10%", cut(1, 10)),
+        ("cut at 50%", cut(1, 2)),
+        ("cut at 90%", cut(9, 10)),
+        (
+            "last byte dropped",
+            b.get(..b.len().saturating_sub(1))
+                .unwrap_or_default()
+                .to_vec(),
+        ),
+        (
+            "NaN vertex",
+            edit_record(&t, "8 Vertices In Brep", 5, |_| "nan".into()).into_bytes(),
+        ),
+        (
+            "inf vertex",
+            edit_record(&t, "8 Vertices In Brep", 5, |_| "inf".into()).into_bytes(),
+        ),
+        (
+            "zero zone tolerance",
+            t.replacen(
+                "0.0000100000000000 - Brep ZoneTol3d",
+                "0.0 - Brep ZoneTol3d",
+                1,
+            )
+            .into_bytes(),
+        ),
+        (
+            "negative zone tolerance",
+            t.replacen(
+                "0.0000100000000000 - Brep ZoneTol3d",
+                "-1.0 - Brep ZoneTol3d",
+                1,
+            )
+            .into_bytes(),
+        ),
+        (
+            "NaN zone tolerance",
+            t.replacen(
+                "0.0000100000000000 - Brep ZoneTol3d",
+                "nan - Brep ZoneTol3d",
+                1,
+            )
+            .into_bytes(),
+        ),
+        (
+            "face count 4294967295",
+            t.replacen("6 Faces In Brep", "4294967295 Faces In Brep", 1)
+                .into_bytes(),
+        ),
+        (
+            "face count -1",
+            t.replacen("6 Faces In Brep", "-1 Faces In Brep", 1)
+                .into_bytes(),
+        ),
+        (
+            "face surface index out of range",
+            edit_record(&t, "6 Faces In Brep", 5, |_| "77".into()).into_bytes(),
+        ),
+        (
+            "faceuse face index out of range",
+            edit_record(&t, "12 Faceuses In Brep", 4, |_| "99".into()).into_bytes(),
+        ),
+        ("vertex gap 1.0 (unhealable)", gapped_box(1.0).into_bytes()),
+        (
+            "one face dropped (open shell)",
+            t.replacen("6 Faces In Brep", "5 Faces In Brep", 1)
+                .into_bytes(),
+        ),
+        (
+            "control point count 1e15",
+            t.replacen(
+                "1 Number of Control Points",
+                "1000000000000000 Number of Control Points",
+                1,
+            )
+            .into_bytes(),
+        ),
+    ]
+}
+
+/// What the raw reader and the importer do with each corpus file, pinned.
+/// FINDINGS against the port's reader: it returns `Ok` with an EMPTY B-rep
+/// (no faces) for a blank file, plain text, binary noise and a header with
+/// no body (and for a NaN zone tolerance, which the seam now refuses before
+/// the reader runs); and `Ok` with a closed box whose vertex sits 1.0 off
+/// its edges. An absurd declared count (faces 2^32-1, control points 1e15)
+/// is refused by the port before it allocates (it checks counts against
+/// the bytes left). The importer refuses every one of them (the
+/// empty ones fail the heal guard's empty check -> `Err invalid`; the gap
+/// past `HEAL_GAP_LIMIT` -> `Err invalid`).
+const KNOWN_SMB_VERDICTS: &[(&str, &str, &str)] = &[
+    ("empty file", "Err refused", "Err refused"),
+    ("one space", "Ok faces=0 no measure", "Err invalid"),
+    ("text, not a B-rep", "Ok faces=0 no measure", "Err invalid"),
+    ("binary noise 4 KiB", "Ok faces=0 no measure", "Err invalid"),
+    ("header only", "Ok faces=0 no measure", "Err invalid"),
+    ("future version", "Err refused", "Err refused"),
+    ("cut at 10%", "Err failed", "Err failed"),
+    ("cut at 50%", "Err failed", "Err failed"),
+    ("cut at 90%", "Err failed", "Err failed"),
+    ("last byte dropped", "Ok V=1000.000", "Ok V=1000.000"),
+    ("NaN vertex", "Err failed", "Err failed"),
+    ("inf vertex", "Err failed", "Err failed"),
+    (
+        "zero zone tolerance",
+        "Ok V=1000.000",
+        "Ok V=1000.000 [zone tolerance 0e0 replaced by 1e-4]",
+    ),
+    (
+        "negative zone tolerance",
+        "Ok V=1000.000",
+        "Ok V=1000.000 [zone tolerance -1e0 replaced by 1e-4]",
+    ),
+    ("NaN zone tolerance", "Err refused", "Err refused"),
+    ("face count 4294967295", "Err failed", "Err failed"),
+    ("face count -1", "Err failed", "Err failed"),
+    (
+        "face surface index out of range",
+        "Err failed",
+        "Err failed",
+    ),
+    (
+        "faceuse face index out of range",
+        "Err failed",
+        "Err failed",
+    ),
+    (
+        "vertex gap 1.0 (unhealable)",
+        "Ok V=1000.000",
+        "Err invalid",
+    ),
+    ("one face dropped (open shell)", "Err failed", "Err failed"),
+    ("control point count 1e15", "Err failed", "Err failed"),
+];
+
+#[test]
+fn corrupt_native_files_never_panic_or_hang() {
+    let mut observed = Vec::new();
+    let mut bad_intact = Vec::new();
+    let cube = Measure {
+        volume: 1000.0,
+        min: [0.0; 3],
+        max: [10.0; 3],
+    };
+    for (name, bytes) in corpus() {
+        let (raw, imp, m) = bounded(name, move || {
+            let mut k = SolidcoreKernel::default();
+            let raw = read_smb(&mut k, &bytes);
+            let raw = port_verdict(raw, &mut k);
+            let imp = import_smb(&mut k, &bytes);
+            let notes: Vec<String> = imp
+                .as_ref()
+                .map(|i| i.notes.iter().map(ToString::to_string).collect())
+                .unwrap_or_default();
+            let bbox = imp.as_ref().ok().map(|i| i.brep.clone());
+            let mut imp = port_verdict(imp.map(|i| i.brep), &mut k);
+            if !notes.is_empty() {
+                imp = format!("{imp} [{}]", notes.join("; "));
+            }
+            let bbox = bbox.and_then(|mut b| k.measure(&mut b).ok());
+            (raw, imp, bbox)
+        });
+        println!("{name:<34} read -> {raw:<22} import -> {imp}");
+        if INTACT.contains(&name) {
+            match m {
+                Some(m) if m.bbox_deviation(&cube) <= 1e-9 && (m.volume - 1000.0).abs() <= 1e-9 => {
+                }
+                other => bad_intact.push(format!("{name}: {other:?}")),
+            }
+        }
+        observed.push((name.to_string(), raw, imp));
+    }
+    assert!(
+        bad_intact.is_empty(),
+        "intact files not the exact 10-box: {bad_intact:?}"
+    );
+    let wrong: Vec<_> = observed
+        .iter()
+        .filter(|(n, _, i)| {
+            if INTACT.contains(&n.as_str()) {
+                !i.starts_with("Ok V=1000.000")
+            } else {
+                i.starts_with("Ok")
+            }
+        })
+        .collect();
+    assert!(
+        wrong.is_empty(),
+        "importer verdict wrong (corrupt model handed out, or intact one lost): {wrong:?}"
+    );
+    let pinned: Vec<(String, String, String)> = KNOWN_SMB_VERDICTS
+        .iter()
+        .map(|(n, r, i)| ((*n).to_string(), (*r).to_string(), (*i).to_string()))
+        .collect();
+    assert_eq!(
+        observed, pinned,
+        "reader verdicts changed - re-triage the findings"
+    );
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn seam_refuses_degenerate_heal_and_oversized_files() {
+    let mut k = SolidcoreKernel::default();
+    let r = k.heal(Brep::new());
+    assert!(
+        matches!(r, Err(KernelError::InvalidInput { op: "heal", .. })),
+        "heal(empty): {:?}",
+        r.map(|_| "Ok")
+    );
+    // an open sheet is not a solid, before or after healing
+    let sheet = solidcore::primitive::api_primitives::create_plane(
+        &mut k.k,
+        solidcore::math::Point3::new(0.0, 0.0, 0.0),
+        10.0,
+        10.0,
+    );
+    assert!(sheet.is_ok(), "fixture sheet not built: {sheet:?}");
+    let sheet = sheet.unwrap_or_default();
+    assert!(!sheet.faces().is_empty(), "fixture sheet has no face");
+    let (k, r) = bounded("heal sheet", move || {
+        let r = k.heal(sheet).map(|_| "Ok");
+        (k, r)
+    });
+    let mut k = k;
+    println!("heal(sheet) -> {r:?}");
+    assert!(r.is_err(), "heal(sheet) came back Ok");
+    let big = vec![b' '; MAX_SMB_BYTES + 1];
+    let r = read_smb(&mut k, &big);
+    assert!(
+        matches!(r, Err(KernelError::InvalidInput { op: "read_smb", .. })),
+        "oversized: {:?}",
+        r.map(|_| "Ok")
+    );
+}
+
+/// The heal guard on the B-rep tolerance, reached directly: a 10-box whose
+/// tolerance is zero, negative, NaN or infinite is refused by name before
+/// the port's heal runs (its stitch doubles the tolerance from a tenth of
+/// it and would never end from zero - upstream HANG-24). Every call runs
+/// under the time bound, since an unguarded port call could spin.
+#[test]
+fn heal_refuses_nonsense_brep_tolerance() {
+    for tol in [0.0, -1.0, f64::NAN, f64::INFINITY] {
+        let r = bounded("heal at nonsense tolerance", move || {
+            let mut k = SolidcoreKernel::default();
+            let mut b = k.make_box([0.0; 3], [10.0; 3])?;
+            b.set_tolerance(tol);
+            k.heal(b).map(|_| "Ok")
+        });
+        println!("heal at tolerance {tol} -> {r:?}");
+        assert!(
+            matches!(r, Err(KernelError::InvalidInput { op: "heal", .. })),
+            "heal at tolerance {tol}: {r:?}"
+        );
+    }
+}

@@ -0,0 +1,98 @@
+## #27 - M12.1 stage 3: healing seam op and the solidcore-side importer corpus
+
+**1. `heal` joins the seam; truck answers `Unsupported`.** The `Kernel` trait
+gains `heal(solid) -> solid`. solidcore runs the port's `api_heal_brep`
+(SMLib's whole heal sequence); truck has no B-rep healing in truck-modeling /
+truck-shapeops 0.4, so it returns `Unsupported` by name and the bench records
+it as "not yet", never as agreement. Dropped: a truck "heal" built from
+mesh welding (truck-meshalgo) - it would heal the tessellation, not the
+B-rep, and would make the two columns compare different things.
+
+**2. The seam judges the heal by its result.** The port's heal reports
+success whatever its healer found (SMLib's `HealBrep` ignores every status
+but "unported"). So the seam refuses an empty B-rep and a B-rep whose
+tolerance is not finite and > 0 up front (the port's stitch doubles its
+tolerance from a tenth of the B-rep's - upstream HANG-24 never ends from
+zero), and afterwards requires the integrity check, a closed manifold
+solid, a positive finite measure and a vertex-edge gap under the limit
+(next point).
+
+**3. `HEAL_GAP_LIMIT = 1e-3` mm (one micron).** Bench reading: the port heals a
+vertex-edge gap of ANY size (1e-6 up to 1.0 on a 10-box) by growing the
+vertex tolerance to cover it, never by moving the vertex. A healed model
+whose vertex sits 1 mm off its edges is not one a toolpath may trust, so the
+seam measures the largest vertex-to-curve-end distance after healing and
+refuses a gap past 1e-3 mm. The value is a CHOSEN bench limit, not a
+sourced one: it passes the sub-micron gaps of the bench fixtures and sits
+under any machining tolerance CamCraft uses. It is to be revisited against
+real-world models (#27 remaining list, item 4). Cost to change: one
+constant; making it a per-import parameter is a later step when a
+production importer exists.
+
+Edges with no 3D curve (a boolean's intersection edges can carry only UV
+trims) have no curve end to measure. `vertex_gaps` COUNTS them as
+`unjudged_edges` instead of passing over them. `import_smb` refuses a model
+with any unjudged edge: a file's edges carry 3D curves (the port's writer
+writes one per edge; all five round-trip fixtures, the L union included,
+read back with zero unjudged edges), so an unjudged edge in a file is
+itself a defect. The seam's `heal` on an in-memory solid still accepts
+them: the port's own boolean results (the L union) carry such edges, they
+were made by the port's intersector rather than read from a file, and the
+integrity and closed-manifold checks have passed on them. That is the
+remaining risk, recorded here: a gap on a curve-less edge of an in-memory
+solid is not measured.
+
+**4. The importer corpus uses the port's own native format (`.smb`).**
+solidcore 1.0.1 reads SMLib's ASCII B-rep files (`read_from_file`), the only
+format it reads without truck; STEP stays on truck-stepio as the issue
+says. The corpus is made from the port's own writer output (the 10-box),
+edited: blank, foreign text, noise, header only, truncations, NaN/inf
+vertex, zero/negative/NaN zone tolerance, nonsense counts and indices, a
+dropped face, an unhealable gap. Every case runs under a 60 s time bound on
+its own thread, so a hang fails the test instead of stalling the gate.
+Verdicts (raw reader and importer) are pinned in a table, like stages 1-2.
+Dropped: a corpus of third-party `.smb` files - none are in-tree and the
+port's upstream test files are not ours to vendor.
+
+**5. Whole edits import, with a note; a future version is refused.** A
+dropped final newline and a zero or negative zone tolerance leave the model
+whole: the importer hands out exactly the closed-form box (volume AND
+bounding box, asserted). The tolerance substitution is not silent (Prime
+Directive, "log diagnostics"): `import_smb` returns `Imported { brep,
+notes }`, and a declared zone tolerance the reader did not take as written
+(replaced, or clamped) becomes `ImportNote::ZoneToleranceReplaced {
+declared, used }`. The kernel crate carries no logging dependency, so the
+note is returned for the caller to show, and the corpus pins its text
+("zone tolerance 0e0 replaced by 1e-4"). A non-finite declared zone
+tolerance is refused by name before the reader runs.
+
+A file whose `Version` is newer than the port's writer version
+(`DATABASE_VERSION`, 42) is now REFUSED, not noted. Reason: the reader
+parses a newer layout with version-42 rules; the corpus file only read
+right because its body is a version-42 body under a changed number. A real
+newer file could read as a subtly different model - the silent wrong answer
+the Prime Directive forbids. Dropped: accepting with a note (output right
+today only by accident of the fixture).
+
+**5a. Allocation from declared counts.** Checked in the port (solidcore
+1.0.1): the reader bounds every declared record count against the bytes left
+in the input before it allocates (`topology::brep_data` `checked_count`, its
+module docs say so; NURBS curve and surface reads call `ensure_available`
+with the declared value count before sizing the arrays). With the seam's 64
+MiB cap on the input, an allocation is therefore bounded by the file size.
+The corpus pins two absurd counts refused that way, quickly and without a
+large allocation: face count 2^32-1 and a curve control-point count of
+1e15.
+
+**6. Writer identities.** The port's writer keeps only the surfaces whose
+recorded owner equals the face's identity; a B-rep the port built names its
+faces its own way, so the seam's writer uses each face's surface owner as
+the face identity. Without it the writer emitted "0 Surfaces" and the read
+back failed - found while building the round trip, not a port defect.
+
+**Findings against the port (pinned, not papered over):** the raw reader
+returns `Ok` with an EMPTY B-rep for a blank file, plain text, binary noise
+and a header with no body (and for a NaN zone tolerance, which the seam now
+refuses before the reader runs); and `Ok` with a closed box whose vertex
+sits 1.0 off its edges. The importer refuses all of them. No panic and no
+hang on any corpus file.
